Roy Cooper

DEM candidate for US Senate, North Carolina · Open seat

Former Governor of North Carolina

Roy Cooper is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in North Carolina. He was governor of North Carolina from 2017 to 2025. Before that he was the state's attorney general from 2001 to 2017 and served in the state General Assembly from 1987 to 2001.

Where Cooper stands

Hurricane Helene recovery / FEMA
Says western North Carolina has received only about 15% of the federal recovery funding it needs. Pledges to work with anyone to get the region the resources it needs to rebuild.
Cost of living / inflation
Proposes a 'Make Stuff Cost Less' plan that includes rolling back tariffs, ending the war in Iran, restoring health care coverage, and stopping insurers from denying care a doctor says is needed.
Military spending / health care
Says health care premiums have risen and supports restoring health care coverage. Supports barring insurance companies from denying coverage for care a doctor says a patient needs.
Immigration enforcement
Says the administration has strengthened the southern border but argues enforcement is targeting people based on appearance. Supports focusing federal resources on fighting crime and deporting violent criminals.
Energy, climate and data centers
Says communities should have the final say on data center projects, including moratoriums. Says developers should pay the full cost of the power they use.
Foreign policy
Supports ending the war in Iran. Has said he worries U.S. involvement could become a 'forever war.'
